Q3529064.label: Timothy Harris
Q3529064.summary: Timothy Sylvester Harris is a Kittitian politician who served as the third prime minister of Saint Kitts and Nevis from 2015 to 2022. He previously served as Minister of Foreign Affairs from 10 August 2001 to 25 January 2008, as Minister of Finance from 2008 to 2010, and as Senior Minister and Minister for Agriculture from 2010 to 2013. Originally affiliated with the Labour Party, he founded and has served as leader of the People's Labour Party since 2013.

Q9576.label: James Callaghan
Q9576.desc: former prime minister of the United Kingdom (1912–2005)
Q9576.summary: Leonard James Callaghan, Baron Callaghan of Cardiff was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1976 to 1979 and Leader of the Labour Party from 1976 to 1980. Callaghan is the only person to have held all four Great Offices of State, having also served as Chancellor of the Exchequer from 1964 to 1967, Home Secretary from 1967 to 1970 and Foreign Secretary from 1974 to 1976. He was a member of Parliament (MP) from 1945 to 1987.

Q3586920.label: 1979 Swiss federal election
Q3586920.desc: election to the federal parliament in Switzerland
Q3586920.summary: Federal elections were held in Switzerland on 21 October 1979. The Social Democratic Party and the Free Democratic Party emerged as the largest parties in the National Council, both winning 51 of the 200 seats.

Q3051880.label: 1957 Polish legislative election
Q3051880.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 20 January 1957. They were the second election to the Sejm – the unicameral parliament of the People's Republic of Poland, and the third ever in the history of Communist Poland. They took place during the liberalization period, following Władysław Gomułka's ascension to power. Although conducted in a more liberal atmosphere than previous elections, they were far from free.

Q29032.label: Miloš Zeman
Q29032.desc: Czech politician, president of the Czech Republic from 2013 to 2023
Q29032.summary: Miloš Zeman is a Czech politician who served as the third president of the Czech Republic from 2013 to 2023. He also previously served as the prime minister of the Czech Republic from 1998 to 2002. As leader of the Czech Social Democratic Party from 1993 to 2001, he is credited with the revival of the party into one of the country's major political forces.

Q4179816.label: Slovak referendum
Q4179816.summary: A referendum was held in Slovakia on 23 May and 24 May 1997. Voters in Slovakia were asked four separate questions: on whether the country should join NATO, whether nuclear weapons should be allowed in Slovakia, whether foreign military bases should be allowed in Slovakia, and whether the President should be elected directly.

Q437096.label: Ingrida Šimonytė
Q437096.desc: Prime Minister of the Republic of Lithuania
Q437096.summary: Ingrida Šimonytė is a Lithuanian politician, public servant, and economist who served as the 17th prime minister of Lithuania from 2020 to 2024. She has been a Member of the Seimas for the Antakalnis constituency since 2016 and was Minister of Finance in the second Kubilius cabinet from 2009 until 2012.

Q1164648.label: 1954 Turkish general election
Q1164648.desc: general election held in the Republic of Turkey in 1954
Q1164648.summary: General elections were held in Turkey on 2 May 1954. The electoral system used was the multiple non-transferable vote. The result was a landslide victory for the Democrat Party, which won 503 of the 541 seats. Voter turnout was 88.6%.

Q1789288.label: Turkish referendum, 1988
Q1789288.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Turkey on 25 September 1988. The proposed changes to the constitution would have led to the 1989 local elections being held a year early. However, they were voted down, with 65% of voters against. Turnout was 88.8%.

Q629096.label: Battle of Kalbajar
Q629096.img: Azerbaijani refugees from Karabakh during the war 15.jpg
Q629096.summary: The Battle of Kalbajar took place in March and April 1993, during the First Nagorno-Karabakh War. It resulted in the capture of the Kalbajar District of Azerbaijan by Armenian military forces.

Q696168.label: Mariana and Palau Islands campaign
Q696168.desc: 1944 military campaign by United States against Imperial Japanese in the Mariana Islands and Palau during the Pacific War
Q696168.summary: The Mariana and Palau Islands campaign, also known as Campaign Plan Granite II, was an offensive launched by the United States against Imperial Japanese forces in the Pacific between June and November 1944 during the Pacific War. The campaign consisted of Operation Forager, which captured the Mariana Islands, and Operation Stalemate, which captured Palau. Q42886504.label: Operation Silver City
Q42886504.desc: 1966 action by the US army in South Vietnam
Q42886504.img: US 173rd Airborne paratroopers near the Song Be March 1966.jpg
Q42886504.summary: Operation Silver City was an operation conducted by the 1st Brigade, 1st Infantry Division and the 173rd Airborne Brigade in Biên Hòa Province, lasting from 7 to 23 March 1966.

Q15359336.label: Adra massacre
Q15359336.desc: 2013 massacre during the Syrian Civil War
Q15359336.summary: The Adra massacre was the killing of at least 32 Alawite, Christian, Druze and Ismailite civilians in the industrial town of Adra, Syria in December 2013, during the Syrian Civil War. According to the government and activists it was conducted by the al-Nusra Front. The U.S. State Department condemned the massacres in Syria including the massacre of civilians in Adra.

mentions.c: Part of Syrian civil war; 32 deaths

Q18639208.label: Fall of Hīt
Q18639208.summary: The Fall of Hīt was the capture of the important Iraqi town of Hīt by IS, which cut off the road leading to nearby Haditha.

Q19678056.label: Second Battle of Idlib
Q19678056.summary: The Battle of Idlib was a military operation in the Idlib Governorate, during the Syrian civil war, conducted by rebels against Syrian government forces defending Idlib city.

Q124077416.label: 2 January 2024 Russian strikes on Ukraine
Q124077416.desc: airstrikes during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
Q124077416.img: Destructions in Orikhiv after Russian attack, 2024-01-02 (01).jpg
Q124077416.summary: Russia has launched waves of missile and drone strikes against energy in Ukraine as part of its invasion. From 2022 the strikes targeted civilian areas beyond the battlefield, particularly critical power infrastructure, which is considered a war crime. By mid-2024 the country only had a third of pre-war electricity generating capacity, and some gas distribution and district heating had been hit.

Q123555176.summary: In the Gaza war, as part of the bombing and invasion of Gaza, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has conducted numerous airstrikes in densely populated Palestinian refugee camps in both the Gaza Strip and West Bank.

Q220008.label: Anthony Giddens, Baron Giddens
Q220008.img: Anthony Giddens at the Progressive Governance Converence, Budapest, Hungary, 2004 October.jpg
Q220008.summary: Anthony Giddens, Baron Giddens is an English sociologist who is known for his theory of structuration and his holistic view of modern societies. He is the author of more than 34 books and was listed, in 2007, as the fifth most cited author in the humanities. He has held academic appointments at universities across the world and has received numerous honorary degrees.

Q5869416.summary: The National Convergence Front was a right-wing political party in Guatemala.

Q1553256.label: Nicaraguan Civil War of 1926–1927
Q1553256.summary: The Nicaraguan Civil War of 1926–1927, or the Constitutionalist War, broke out after a coup d'état by Emiliano Chamorro, a member of the Conservative Party, removed Nicaragua's democratically elected government, resulting in a rebellion by members of the Liberal Party. The conflict came to an end after a military and diplomatic intervention by the United States resulted in the Pact of Espino Negro, which began the Peace of Tipitapa.

Q15860072.label: Russo-Ukrainian war
Q15860072.desc: armed conflict between Russia and Ukraine since 2014
aliases: Special operation on the territory of Ukraine
Q15860072.summary: The Russo-Ukrainian war began in February 2014 and is ongoing. Following Ukraine's Revolution of Dignity, Russia occupied Crimea and annexed it from Ukraine. It then supported Russian separatist armed groups who started a war in the eastern Donbas region against Ukraine's military. In 2018, Ukraine declared the region to be occupied by Russia. The first eight years of conflict also involved naval incidents and cyberwarfare.

Participants: International Legion of Territorial Defense of Ukraine

Q907112.label: Transnistria
Q907112.desc: unrecognized state in the international borders of Moldova
Q907112.summary: Transnistria, officially known as the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic (PMR) and locally as Pridnestrovie, is a landlocked breakaway state internationally recognised as part of Moldova. Transnistria controls most of the narrow strip of land between the Dniester river and the Moldova–Ukraine border, as well as some land on the other side of the river's bank. Its capital and largest city is Tiraspol. Transnistria is officially designated by the Republic of Moldova as the Administrative-Territorial Units of the Left Bank of the Dniester or as Stînga Nistrului.
